mem.t: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

lessons.title: Unless the Lord Builds
lessons.theme: The worth of our labour lies in whether God himself is building

v: Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

lessons.still: Think of the thing that has made you busiest and most anxious lately. Place it before the Lord and ask, “Lord, are you building this, or am I?” Then relax your shoulders and admit, “Without you, it is all in vain.”
teach: Workers on a building site may carry bricks and lay walls, but without the architect’s blueprint, the faster they build, the harder it will fall. The psalmist uses the word “vain” three times: the builders labour in vain, the watchman guards in vain, rising early and staying up late is in vain. He is not telling people not to work; he is saying that work done apart from God is wasted effort.

“He gives sleep to his loved ones.” The contrast in this verse is stark: on one side, anxiously rising early and staying up late; on the other, peaceful sleep. God does not reward laziness with sleep; he uses sleep to show that he is the one who truly builds. While I sleep, God does not; the world keeps turning in his hands.

This week we learn the rhythm of family and work. Many Christians’ problem is not that they don’t work hard, but that they work too hard — treating themselves as the builder of everything. A change of mindset: from “It all depends on me” to “I work together with God, and God is the builder.” Being able to sleep in peace is itself an expression of faith.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let people be people and let God be God. Anxiety is often an expression of the self-ruled life — I think I have to hold everything together. People living the self-emptied life return to their place, doing what people should do and letting God do what God does. Building God’s kingdom system begins with letting God be the builder.
q: Who is God? — “He gives sleep to his loved ones” — what does this show you about God’s love?
Who am I? — Do you treat yourself as the builder of everything in your life?
How shall I respond? — How will you express your trust tonight by “sleeping in peace”?
lessons.jesus: While the disciples panicked in the storm, Jesus was asleep in the stern on a cushion. It was not that he didn’t care; he trusted the Father completely. He woke, rebuked the wind and the waves, and they stopped, and there was a great calm. In his presence, we too can sleep in peace.
lessons.pray: God who built all things, I confess that I often think everything depends on me, rising early and staying up late, anxious and restless. Today I hand my work, my family and my future over to you. Be the builder, so that I can work together with you and sleep in peace in your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Go to bed thirty minutes earlier than usual tonight, and before sleeping hand tomorrow over to God
Before you start work, pray: “Lord, please build this yourself.”
Share with one of “my 2” something you are learning to entrust to God
lessons.noon: “Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain.” — Lord, right now please build this yourself.

lessons.title: Work Is God’s Calling
lessons.theme: Work is not a curse but a trust: working together with God

v: The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.

lessons.still: Picture where you will work today: a desk, a kitchen, a classroom, a building site, or your home. Quietly invite the Lord into that place: “Lord, that place is yours too. Today I go there to work for you.”
teach: Many people see work as a punishment for the Fall, and Monday as the start of the week’s misery. Yet before humanity sinned, God “put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.” Work was God’s original design, not the result of sin. Sin brought thorns and sweat, but work itself is a good trust.

Paul wrote to the slaves of his day — the lowest-ranking workers in society — “Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men.” Even a slave’s work could become service to God, because “you serve the Lord Christ.” Your boss sees your performance; the Lord sees your heart.

A change of mindset: there is no division between “spiritual work” and “secular work,” only between work done “for the Lord” and work done “for myself.” Cleaning, bookkeeping, teaching, caring for children — all of it can be worship. When work becomes a calling, we no longer work to prove ourselves, nor do we procrastinate to escape it.
lessons.light: 321 Light: A shift in perspective — from the worldly to the godly. On the path of service, serving means letting Jesus reign and serving by his authority. When we let Jesus reign in the workplace, our work becomes a place for building God’s kingdom system. The glory is not mine; it belongs to Jesus.
q: Who is God? — God himself is at work in creating, sustaining and redeeming — how does this shape the way you see your own work?
Who am I? — Do you work for the Lord, for other people’s approval, or to prove yourself?
How shall I respond? — In which task today will you work “as for the Lord”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “My Father is still working, so I am working too” (John 5:17). In Nazareth he worked as a carpenter, making ploughs and yokes with his hands; in his ministry he went through all the towns and villages. His work was never for his own name, but to finish what the Father had entrusted to him.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for entrusting work to me. Forgive me for so often complaining about my work, or treating it as a place to prove myself. Today, whatever I do, I will work at it with all my heart, as for you. Reign in my work. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before you start work, write: “Today I am working for the Lord.”
Wholeheartedly complete a piece of work no one will notice
Say a word of thanks for their hard work to one of “my 2” (a colleague or family member)
lessons.noon: “And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men” — Lord, right now I do this for you.

lessons.title: The Priority of Family
lessons.theme: The family is the first spiritual community God established

v: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart;
and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
But if anyone doesn’t provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

lessons.still: In your heart, bring each member of your family to mind, one by one. Pause quietly at each name and ask the Lord, “Lord, lately have I been giving them my best time, or my leftover time?”
teach: Many people give their best energy to work and bring their leftover exhaustion home — like a chef who prepares a banquet for customers at the restaurant, then goes home and feeds the family instant noodles. That is not God’s intention. Before the tabernacle and the temple, God first established the family in Eden.

Moses commanded that God’s words be taught “diligently to your children, and… when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.” Passing on the faith does not happen only once a week in a church building, but at the dinner table, on the road, and at bedtime. Paul puts it even more seriously: whoever does not provide for his own household “is worse than an unbeliever.”

The order of relationships: first with God, then with myself, then with others, then with things. Our family are the “others” closest to us, and they come before things. This doesn’t mean work is unimportant, but work should not swallow up the family. A change of mindset: the family is not an obstacle to ministry; it is the first workshop of ministry.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. The family is the most real training ground for 920 — my family are my closest 2. Living the self-emptied life at home is harder than living it on the platform, and more genuine. A family built on God’s word is itself part of God’s kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — God established the family before he established the temple — what does this show you about what God values?
Who am I? — Are you giving your family your best time, or your leftover time?
How shall I respond? — What uninterrupted time will you set aside for your family this week?
lessons.jesus: In the terrible agony of the cross, Jesus still saw his mother and entrusted her to the care of the disciple he loved. Even at the moment of completing the great work of redemption, he did not neglect his family. His ministry never came at the cost of sacrificing his family.
lessons.pray: Father, thank you for giving me a family. Forgive me for so often giving my family my leftover time. Help me, at the table, on the road and at bedtime, to bring your word and your love to my family. Reign in my home. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Share a meal with your family today without looking at your phone
Before bed, pray briefly for each member of your family
Say a word of thanks or apology to one of “my 2” (a family member)
lessons.noon: “These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart.” — Lord, right now let your word live in my home.

lessons.title: Rest in the Midst of Work
lessons.theme: Only one thing is needed: sitting at the Lord’s feet

v: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,

lessons.still: Stop what you are doing, and sit at the Lord’s feet like Mary. Do nothing; simply be in his presence. If items from your to-do list pop up, don’t chase them away; just lay them, one by one, at the Lord’s feet.
teach: When your phone’s battery is low, no amount of effort will keep it going for long; you have to plug it in. Martha was a hard-working woman, and preparing a meal for Jesus was a good thing. But she was “anxious and troubled about many things,” to the point of blaming her sister and challenging Jesus. Her problem was not her work; it was that she lost the Lord in the middle of it.

Jesus said, “One thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part.” Isaiah also said, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” Sadly, Israel “refused.” Strength does not come from busyness; it comes from returning to God and being still before him.

Resting in the midst of work does not mean not working; it means keeping our hearts with the Lord while we work. Work can include short pauses: an arrow prayer, a deep breath, a verse of Scripture. A change of mindset: rest is not the reward after the work is finished; it is the source of the work. First sit at the Lord’s feet, then rise to serve.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself — from the heart comes joy, from the head comes worry. Martha lived from her head and grew more troubled the more she did; Mary lived from her heart and received the good part. With our focus on Jesus rather than on tasks, our work can become service that flows from rest.
q: Who is God? — Jesus tenderly called, “Martha, Martha” — how does he see you in your busyness?
Who am I? — In your work or ministry, are you more like Martha or like Mary?
How shall I respond? — What moment of “sitting at the Lord’s feet” will you build into your work today?
lessons.jesus: At the busiest point of Jesus’ ministry, so many people were coming and going that there was no time even to eat, yet he often withdrew to deserted places to pray. He drew strength from the Father, then went out again to serve the crowds. He was busy, but his heart was never in a panic, because his source was in the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I confess that I am often like Martha, anxious and troubled about many things. Call me by name and bring me back to your feet. I choose the good part, and even in my work I will not leave your presence. Be the source of my strength. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set a reminder every three hours to stop and pray a one-line arrow prayer
Write down the things that make you “anxious and troubled,” and hand them to the Lord one by one
Instead of hurrying one of “my 2,” invite them to stop with you for a cup of tea
lessons.noon: “But one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part” — Lord, right now I sit at your feet.

lessons.title: The Rhythm of Day and Night
lessons.theme: The rhythm God has set is a protection for our lives

v: God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.
He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

lessons.still: Notice your breathing: in and out, in and out. Life has a rhythm built into it. Quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, is the rhythm of my life within your design, or has it lost its balance?”
teach: The heart contracts and relaxes; breathing goes in and out; land is farmed and then left fallow. This week we have seen that God is the builder (Day 1), that work is a calling (Day 2), the priority of family (Day 3), and rest in the midst of work (Day 4). Today we learn the rhythm God has set.

Genesis says, “There was evening and there was morning, the first day.” For the Hebrews, the day began in the evening — first rest, then work. While we sleep, God is already at work. Jesus also said to his busy disciples, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” Rest is not laziness; it is the Lord’s own invitation.

God established the Sabbath to protect people with time, so that we remember: I am not a machine; I am a child of God. Next week is the Stage 3 retreat week, when we will stop to review the fruit of these thirteen weeks. A change of mindset: rhythm is not wasted time; it is essential for a life that bears lasting fruit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let people be people and let God be God. People who never stop working are often trying to hold up the world in God’s place; those who are willing to stop are acknowledging that God is the one in control. Rest is trust in God, and a form of worship that lets Jesus receive all the glory.
q: Who is God? — God established day and night and the Sabbath — what does this show you about his heart?
Who am I? — Does your life have a rhythm of breathing in and out, or is it all breathing in and never out?
How shall I respond? — What time of rest will you set for yourself and your family this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus himself lived in rhythm: teaching and healing among the crowds by day, going out to deserted places to pray in the early morning; sometimes with the many, sometimes withdrawing with just his disciples. He was never frantic and never stagnant, because his steps were in step with the Father’s heart.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for setting the rhythm of day and night and of Sabbath rest. Forgive me for so often working without resting, as if everything depended on me. I accept your invitation to come apart with you to a deserted place and rest awhile. Reorder the rhythm of my life, and let me find strength in you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set aside a full block of Sabbath rest this week, and put it in your calendar
Turn off your screens before bed tonight, and end the day with thanksgiving
Invite one of “my 2” (a family member or co-worker) to enjoy some time of rest together
lessons.noon: “Come away into a deserted place” — Lord, right now I rest awhile in you.
